{"id": "cf766964-eaa7-4490-b0f2-cce94ca14766", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_EhdffQV2RKRv9GjVQmxrpW", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Api-Bedrock-Agentcore-Control-2023-06-05\",\"context\":\"### CustomJWTAuthorizerConfiguration\\n\\n##### Description\\n\\nConfiguration for inbound JWT-based authorization, specifying how incoming requests should be authenticated.\\n\\n##### Members\\n\\n**advertisedScopeMapping**\\n: : **Type:** *Associative array of custom strings keys (AllowedScopeType) to strings*\\n\\n A map that associates each scope in `allowedScopes` with a corresponding advertised scope value. The advertised scope appears in OAuth protected resource metadata and `WWW-Authenticate` response headers. Use this parameter when the scope that clients request from your identity provider differs from the scope in the validated token. Each key is a scope from `allowedScopes` that the service uses for token validation. Each value is the corresponding scope that the service advertises to clients. Scopes without a mapping entry appear unchanged to clients.\\n\\n**allowedAudience**\\n: : **Type:** *Array of strings*\\n\\n Represents individual audience values that are validated in the incoming JWT token validation process.\\n\\n**allowedClients**\\n: : **Type:** *Array of strings*\\n\\n Represents individual client IDs that are validated in the incoming JWT token validation process.\\n\\n**allowedScopes**\\n: : **Type:** *Array of strings*\\n\\n An array of scopes that are allowed to access the token.\\n\\n**allowedWorkloadConfiguration**\\n: : **Type:** *AllowedWorkloadConfiguration structure*\\n\\n The configuration that restricts which workloads in the request's identity chain are allowed to invoke the target, identified by their hosting environments and workload identities. At launch, this is supported only for AgentCore Runtime targets, and the allowed workloads are AgentCore Gateways.\\n\\n**certificateConfigurations**\\n: : **Type:** *Array of CertificateConfiguration structures*\\n\\n The private certificate authority (CA) configurations for the identity provider. Use this to have AgentCore Identity trust a private CA when establishing TLS connections to identity provider endpoints. You can specify only one certificate authority configuration in this list. Provide the certificate by reference to an Amazon S3 object or an Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager secret. You can use this only together with `privateEndpoint`.\\n\\n**customClaims**\\n: : **Type:** *Array of CustomClaimValidationType structures*\\n\\n An array of objects that define a custom claim validation name, value, and operation\\n\\n**discoveryUrl**\\n: : **Required**: *Yes*\\n : **Type:** *string*\\n\\n This URL is used to fetch OpenID Connect configuration\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-sdk-php/v3/api/api-bedrock-agentcore-control-2023-06-05.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Set up inbound authorization for your gateway\",\"context\":\"### Configure a JWT authorizer\\n\\nCreate an application and client with a supported identity provider. For an Amazon Cognito example, see Get started with Amazon Cognito. Note the OpenID Connect (OIDC) or OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata (RFC 8414) discovery URL and client ID.\\n\\nRun the following command in an AgentCore project directory:\\n\\n```\\nagentcore add gateway \\\\\\n --name MyGateway \\\\\\n --protocol-type MCP \\\\\\n --authorizer-type CUSTOM_JWT \\\\\\n --authorizer-configuration '{\\n \\\"customJwtAuthorizer\\\": {\\n \\\"discoveryUrl\\\": \\\"<DISCOVERY_URL>\\\",\\n \\\"allowedClients\\\": [\\\"<CLIENT_ID>\\\"]\\n }\\n }'\\n```\\n\\nThe AgentCore CLI uses the configuration of your existing identity provider. To invoke the gateway, obtain an access token from your provider. For Amazon Cognito, see The token issuer endpoint in the Amazon Cognito Developer Guide\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-inbound-auth.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Configure inbound JWT authorizer\",\"context\":\"# Configure inbound JWT authorizer\\n\\nThe inbound authorizer authenticates and authorizes incoming OAuth 2.0 API requests to AgentCore Runtime and AgentCore Gateway. It validates JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) before allowing access to agents or gateways. The authorizer is Identity Provider (IdP) agnostic and works with any OAuth 2.0 compatible identity provider. When AgentCore Runtime or AgentCore Gateway receives an inbound request, the authorizer will use the configured discovery URL to fetch the public keys and authorization server endpoint to perform the JWT validation. You can configure the authorizer based on your IdP and allowed authorization scopes or claims\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/inbound-jwt-authorizer.html\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"How do I resolve the \\\"Authorization method mismatch\\\" error that I receive when I invoke my AgentCore Runtime agent?\",\"context\":\"### Invoke a runtime that you configured for JWT\\n\\nTo invoke a runtime that uses JWT authorization, send an HTTPS request with a bearer token in the **Authorization** header. For example, run the following command:\\n\\n```plaintext\\ncurl -X POST \\\"https://bedrock-agentcore.example-region.amazonaws.com/runtimes/example-encoded-runtime-arn/invocations?qualifier=DEFAULT\\\" \\\\\\n -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer example-access-token\\\" \\\\\\n -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n -H \\\"X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id: example-session-id\\\" \\\\\\n -d '{\\\"prompt\\\": \\\"Hello\\\"}'\\n```\\n\\n**Note:** Replace **example-region** with your AWS Region. Replace **example-encoded-runtime-arn** with your URL-encoded runtime ARN. Replace **example-access-token** with an access token from your identity provider. Replace **example-session-id** with a session ID that's 33-256 characters long. If you use an endpoint other than **DEFAULT**, then replace **DEFAULT** with your endpoint name.\\n\\nTo get an access token and URL-encode the runtime ARN, see [Step 5: Use bearer token to invoke your agent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-oauth.html#oauth-invoke-agent)\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-resolve-authorization-method\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"aws-auth\",\"skill_description\":\"Adds user authentication to web and mobile apps with Amazon Cognito (user pools and identity pools) and the AWS Amplify client auth libraries. **Authorizer settings on the seven runtimes**
- **Six runtimes have no JWT authorizer.** These are the five `llmops_eval_*` runtimes (support, search, orders, catalog, billing) and `cost_estimator_agent`. A runtime with no custom JWT authorizer expects AWS SigV4 (IAM) credentials. I'm inferring that from the empty configuration. A bearer token sent to one of them is rejected however valid it is. AWS documents this as an "Authorization method mismatch" error.
- **One runtime has a JWT authorizer, and it points at Cognito.** `cost_estimator_agent_with_identity` has a discovery URL for the Cognito user pool `us-east-1_5OBP5otjw` and allows one client ID, `2es2efs8h5riq5s6cu0n2a7tjf`. It has no audience, scope or custom-claim rules. The authorizer fetches signing keys from the discovery URL, so tokens from your IdP will fail on signature and issuer.

**What to check next**
1. **Runtime and authorizer.** Confirm which runtime your web app calls. Its authorizer must have a `discoveryUrl` for your IdP's `/.well-known/openid-configuration`. That URL must be publicly reachable, and its issuer must match the token's `iss`.
2. **Audience and client ID.** AgentCore checks `allowedAudience` against the token's `aud` claim. It checks `allowedClients` against the `client_id` claim. Some IdPs put the client ID only in `aud`, or only in `azp`. If your tokens have no `client_id` claim, an `allowedClients` rule will reject every request. Configure `allowedAudience` instead.
3. **Token type.** Send the access token, not the ID token, unless your `aud` or client rules are written for the ID token.
4. **Scopes and custom claims.** If `allowedScopes` or `customClaims` are set, the token must satisfy all of them.
5. **Request format.** Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` over HTTPS to the runtime invocation endpoint. The session ID header must be 33–256 characters.

If your runtime lives in another account or Region, I can look there too. Tell me which runtime your app calls. You can also paste the decoded token claims with the signature removed: `iss`, `aud`, `client_id` or `azp`, `scope`, `exp`. Then I can compare them against the authorizer settings.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
